title: NQCC Releases QCTI Phase 1 Report as Seven Quantum Testbeds Advance to Full-Scale Evaluation - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The NQCC/Innovate UK QCTI Phase 1 Report confirms seven commercial quantum testbeds commissioned at Harwell under a £30M SBRI award, with the NQCC acting as 'alpha customer'; Phase 2 independent benchmarking with Edinburgh's Quantum Software Lab runs through Q2 2027. Participating companies raised ~$715M in venture funding in 2025, and the report lists detailed specs (e.g., Oxford Ionics >10 s coherence, QuEra >200 qubits, Rigetti 36-qubit upgrade).

insights.claim: The UK's Quantum Computing Testbed Initiative was financed through a £30 million SBRI award that made the NQCC an institutional 'alpha customer' for seven commercial quantum testbeds at Harwell.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A small public outlay buys first-customer status and comparative evaluation across vendors.
insights.locator: The UK’s National Quantum Computing Centre

insights.claim: Companies in the QCTI testbed cohort raised about $715 million in private venture funding in 2025 alone, which the report presents as catalytic impact of the lead-customer model.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Suggests ~£30M of government purchasing correlated with ~20x private capital raised; useful precedent for valuing government-anchor deals.
insights.quote: raised approximately $715 million in private venture funding in 2025 alone

insights.claim: IonQ's acquisition of Oxford Ionics is cited as a major consolidation event among the UK testbed participants.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: US acquirers are buying UK testbed-validated vendors, a consolidation trend relevant to M&A theses.

insights.claim: Follow-on UK Quantum Mission Pilot grants added £4.6 million to participating consortia for sub-system scaling, on-chip cryogenic readout and real-time decoding pipelines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows continued non-dilutive funding flowing to testbed vendors beyond the initial contract.

insights.claim: QuEra established a dedicated UK operating subsidiary and campus-co-located facility, including its own cleanroom, while the other six testbeds were commissioned in NQCC-managed halls.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Foreign vendors are making physical UK investments to win sovereign procurement positioning.

insights.claim: The Oxford Ionics (IonQ) QuARTET trapped-ion testbed achieved over 10 s coherence times and 99.97(3)% SPAM fidelity, with a chassis designed for in-field QPU upgrades up to 256 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: In-field upgradeability lowers customer replacement cost and is a competitive differentiator in procurement.
insights.quote: achieved > 10 s coherence times, 99.97(3)% SPAM fidelity

insights.claim: QuEra UK's Generation-4 neutral-atom system uses a zoned shuttling architecture with over 200 physical qubits across 2,000 register sites, >99% atom initialization and 150 μs shuttling times.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Neutral atoms lead on raw qubit counts among the testbeds; shuttling speed is the key throughput constraint to watch.
insights.quote: > 200 physical qubits across 2,000 register sites with > 99% atom initialization and 150 μs shuttling times

insights.claim: Infleqtion UK's Sqale testbed uses a 16×16 neutral-atom site geometry with Rydberg entanglement to deliver a 100-qubit system with universal gates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Second neutral-atom vendor in the program, intensifying modality competition.

insights.claim: Rigetti UK's testbed was upgraded from a 24-qubit 4×6 lattice to 36 qubits (6×6) with 38 tunable couplers, integrated with Riverlane's Deltaflow decoder for real-time error correction, after a nine-month deployment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Superconducting qubit counts here trail neutral atoms; the Riverlane decoder integration matters for QEC software positioning.

insights.claim: Quantum Motion's QM One is a silicon spin-qubit QPU manufactured on industrial 300 mm CMOS foundry wafers, with automated drift calibration compatible with Qiskit, Cirq and PennyLane.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: CMOS-foundry manufacturing is the main scaling argument for silicon spin, potentially leveraging existing semiconductor supply chains.

insights.claim: ORCA Computing's Asteroidea photonic system combines quantum dots, cavity-enhanced SPDC and squeezed vacuum sources with an embedded GPU, and Aegiq's Artemis fits deterministic single-photon sources into standard 19-inch data-center racks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Rack-mount form factors and GPU integration point to photonics vendors pitching data-center compatibility.

insights.claim: QCTI Phase 2, Testbed Technical Evaluation, runs through Q2 2027 with the University of Edinburgh's Quantum Software Lab and will independently verify system-level metrics, study noise dynamics and assess suitability for specific computational classes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Independent verified benchmarks due by mid-2027 could re-rate vendors whose marketing claims diverge from measured performance.

insights.claim: Phase 2 is split into Building Block Projects (error mitigation, syndrome decoding latency, verifiable quantum advantage metrics) and Pipeline Projects mapping Hamiltonian simulation, optimization and quantum machine learning to each modality's strengths.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Matching workloads to modalities implies the UK expects no single winning architecture, favoring a multi-vendor market.
